title: Model Substitutability Live Scorecard & Signal Fusion Playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a live, composable scorecard that quantifies how substitutable each candidate model is for Redwood customers and surface procurement triggers tied to telemetry and market signals. The scorecard will combine performance, latency economics, operational risk, and licensing/availability signals into a single, auditable view used by product, sales, and procurement teams.
scope: Phase 1: design scorecard schema, define signal weighting, and produce an internal dashboard prototype. Phase 2: wire telemetry + billing + vendor availability feeds and create automatic procurement trigger rules. Phase 3: integrate scorecard outputs into the Sourcing Runbook and alerting channels (Slack + Console). Excludes contract negotiation playbooks and legal reviews (handled by Legal).
deliverables: Wireframe for live dashboard (Console mock + Figma link)
Reference implementation: score computation notebook (Python) with sample telemetry
Procurement trigger ruleset (thresholds + actions) and runbook
milestones: M3: Prototype score notebook with synthetic telemetry (2026-03-22)
M4: Ingest billing + telemetry feeds into staging (2026-03-29)
M5: Trigger rules + playbook + internal launch (2026-04-01)
acceptance_criteria: Scorecard computes a substitutability score (0-100) for a minimum of 10 candidate models using live telemetry
Dashboard prototype shows per-customer risk banding, top contributing signals, and time series of score changes
Procurement triggers produce actionable items: email to procurement, autoplace reservation suggestion, or priority flag in ticketing system
A documented runbook exists that maps score thresholds to clear human workflows and escalation paths
Stakeholders (Sales Ops, Procurement lead, Runtime eng) have signed off on signal weightings and thresholds
